config.title: Build generic data table props API

intro.title: Build generic data table props API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a generic props API for a data table component using TypeScript. You'll learn how to use generics to create flexible, type-safe components that can work with any data shape. The main constructs involved are TypeScript generics, interfaces, and type parameters. By the end, you'll have a reusable table component that maintains full type safety for different datasets.
intro.usecase: Generic data table props APIs are essential in enterprise dashboards and admin panels where developers need to display various datasets with consistent UI patterns. For example, an e-commerce analytics dashboard might show customer data, product inventories, and sales reports—all using the same table component with different column definitions and data types. This pattern allows developers to create reusable table components that can handle user data, financial transactions, or inventory items while maintaining type safety across different views. By implementing this API, you can build a single flexible table component instead of creating separate tables for each data type, significantly reducing code duplication in data-intensive applications.

objectives: Construct a generic TypeScript interface for table column definitions
Implement a generic data table component with type-safe props
Apply generic constraints to ensure data objects have required properties
Configure a reusable table component that accepts different data types
Initialize a data table with typed props and sample data
Manipulate column configurations to control display and formatting
Render a type-safe table component with proper TypeScript validation

steps.title: Import React and TypeScript utilities
steps.instruction: Import React and the ReactNode type from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and ReactNode from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:

successCriteria: React and ReactNode are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import React and ReactNode from 'react'.

steps.title: Define the base DataTableProps interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named DataTableProps with a generic type parameter T.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and angle brackets for the generic parameter.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { ReactNode } from 'react';
// Create the DataTableProps interface with generic type parameter T here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a generic interface that will serve as the foundation for your data table component props.
successCriteria: DataTableProps interface is defined with a generic type parameter T.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the 'interface' keyword and including the generic parameter <T>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to create an interface named DataTableProps with a generic type parameter T.

steps.title: Add the data property to the interface
steps.instruction: Add a 'data' property of type T[] to the DataTableProps interface.
steps.hint: Inside the DataTableProps interface, add a property named 'data' with the type T[].
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTableProps interface now includes a 'data' property that will hold the array of generic items.
successCriteria: DataTableProps interface has a property named 'data' with type T[].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a property named 'data' with the correct type T[] inside the DataTableProps interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The data property is missing or incorrect. Please add a 'data' property of type T[] to the DataTableProps interface.

steps.title: Add the columns property to the interface
steps.instruction: Add a 'columns' property to the DataTableProps interface with the type definition: columns: Array<{ key: keyof T; header: string }>
steps.hint: Inside the DataTableProps interface, add a new property named 'columns' with the specified type. This defines how each data column should be rendered.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTableProps interface now includes a 'columns' property that defines the structure for table columns.
successCriteria: The interface contains a 'columns' property with type Array<{ key: keyof T; header: string }>
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a columns property, but check the type definition. It should be: columns: Array<{ key: keyof T; header: string }>
steps.feedbackWrong: The columns property is missing or has incorrect type. Add: columns: Array<{ key: keyof T; header: string }> inside the DataTableProps interface.

steps.title: Define the Column interface
steps.instruction: Create a separate interface named Column to define the structure of each column configuration. It should have key, header, and renderCell properties.
steps.hint: Define an interface with three properties: key (string), header (string), and renderCell (a function that takes an item of type T and returns a ReactNode).
steps.expectedOutcome: A new Column interface is defined with the required properties, ready to be used in the DataTableProps interface.
successCriteria: Column interface is created with key, header, and renderCell properties, each with correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the Column interface, but it's missing some properties or has incorrect types. Check that key, header, and renderCell are all present with the right types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Column interface is not properly defined. Make sure to create an interface named Column with key (string), header (string), and renderCell (function that takes T and returns ReactNode).

steps.title: Make the Column interface generic
steps.instruction: Add a generic type parameter to the existing Column interface and use it in the renderCell property type.
steps.hint: The Column interface should accept the same generic type T as DataTableProps. Update renderCell to use this type for its item parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Column interface now has a generic type parameter T, and renderCell uses (item: T) => React.ReactNode as its type.
successCriteria: Column interface is generic with type parameter T, and renderCell's item parameter is typed as T.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure to add the generic type parameter to Column and update renderCell to use it for the item parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Column interface should be generic. Add a type parameter T to Column and use it in renderCell: (item: T) => React.ReactNode.

steps.title: Connect Column interface to DataTableProps
steps.instruction: Update the columns property in the DataTableProps interface to use the generic Column<T> interface type.
steps.hint: Change the type of the columns property from Column[] to Column<T>[] to connect the generic types.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTableProps interface will have a columns property typed as Column<T>[], connecting the generic type between the two interfaces.
successCriteria: The columns property in DataTableProps is typed as Column<T>[].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using Column<T>[] for the columns property type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The columns property should be typed as Column<T>[] to properly connect the generic types.

steps.title: Add optional loading state property
steps.instruction: Add an optional 'loading' property of type boolean to the DataTableProps interface.
steps.hint: Use a question mark after the property name to make it optional, and specify the type as boolean.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTableProps interface now includes an optional loading property to handle loading states.
successCriteria: DataTableProps has an optional 'loading' property with type boolean.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added 'loading?: boolean' to the DataTableProps interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loading property wasn't added correctly. Check that it's optional (using ?) and has type boolean.

steps.title: Add optional empty state message
steps.instruction: Add an optional 'emptyMessage' property of type string to the DataTableProps interface.
steps.hint: Add a new property with a question mark to make it optional, and specify its type as string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTableProps interface now includes an optional emptyMessage property to customize the message shown when there is no data.
successCriteria: DataTableProps interface has an optional emptyMessage property of type string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but check that it's optional (using '?') and of type string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DataTableProps interface should have an optional emptyMessage property of type string.

steps.instruction: Create a functional component named DataTable that accepts DataTableProps<T> as props and returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a component that uses the generic DataTableProps interface you've built. Use the same generic type parameter T.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DataTable component that accepts DataTableProps<T> and returns null.
successCriteria: DataTable component is defined with generic type parameter T, accepts DataTableProps<T> as props, and returns null.
